questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The focus of national and international views and interpretations of the fight against climate change on an economic, academic level

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience, I met a lot of nice people because of the ESN Amsterdam program, the academic level of the university was intriguing and exciting, overall very happy.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very intuitive, I had a lot of problems with course registrations, but when I asked the university, as well as my own university, there were a lot of people that were happy to help me, and I managed to figure it all out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have spoken a lot to the exchange office, and they were extremely helpful!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing market in Amsterdam is crazy, and I would definitely recommend the housing provided by the UvA through "Lieven de Key". It was really nice, and compared to the stress of others finding housing on their own, this is the way to do it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Communication with my housing provider, "Lieven de Key", is not great, and the rules are kind of strict with regards to partying and social gatherings. However, the facilities are great and the apartments are also really nice. I have heard that this can vary from place to place within the housing agency, but at least where I lived, it was a really enjoyable experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a lot of problems with course registrations, and you will have to be aware about courses on the second block of the spring semester. But again, the university was very helpful with finding courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You fill in a google forms with the courses available that is send via. e-mail, which makes it easy to register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange office were really helpful to help you register for additional courses of necessary.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had 1 out of 6 courses that I didn't really want, but this was because I was to slow to realize that I hadn't registered for the courses on the second block. Even then, the course wasn't that bad.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure if you are going in the spring, that you register for the second block courses as well, when you register for the first block.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The master courses were really nice, the lecturers seemed competent, and you didn't feel out of your comfort zone, even though some of the courses touched on topics that I hadn't encountered before. The bachelor level courses were a bit easier, but still presented some views and topics that were really interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is a lot more about engaging with the students. Many of the courses featured presentations from fellow students, which I hadn't really done a lot of at UCPH. Also, these presentations mostly featured some sort of discussion element, which was actually really nice to try.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Competition Policy
Industrial Organisation
Natural Resource Economics
International Management
Economic Growth
Management and Leadership in the Digital Age

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Competition Policy - You get to apply economic reasoning to real-life cases on EU level, where you have to argue. This helped me a lot to think about how to argue from a specific economic view point, and also engaging in a discussion based on academic reasoning.

Economic Growth - It was basically an extension of the Macro I course from my BA, but it built out the models further than we had done previously, and had a lot of interesting new perspectives. 

Also, all of the courses had some incorporation of the aspect of climate change, which I was really happy about.

questions.answer: Nothing was really unexpected, it seems like the price level overall is lower than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Less expensive overall.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
ESN Amsterdam is a student organisation for exchange students, which held a lot of parties and organized introduction activities. This was really nice, and helped a lot to meeting new people. 

The USC was a sports and fitness institution, that is collaborating with the UvA. This was nice, where you could try new sports, go to the gym, and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ESN parties were really nice, would definitely recommend. Most of the techno clubs around Amsterdam are really nice, even if you are not into techno. 

The museums of Amsterdam are also really nice, but you have reserve tickets in advance.

If you arrive during spring, the Kings Day is such an incredible event, and this would be the highest recommendation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The museums of Amsterdam, the nightlife (Clubs, bars, etc.), Amsterdam also have really lovely parks and streets, so just walking around the city is very nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Danish and dutch culture seems quite similar, so it wasn't that much of a problem. The language is difficult to understand however, but even for this the university offers language courses.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had a hard time socializing with local students, and most of the people I met were also exchange students. But the ones I did meet were really easy to talk to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language, but other than that not much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people here are really friendly, and you always feel welcome wherever you go to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to attend social events.
Make sure you have your course registration planned.
Be aware of the housing market, it can be very bad depending on arrangement (I recommend Lieven de Key through the UvA).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The dutch are known to be quite direct, they don't see it as something rude, even though some people might find it a bit rude. Also, exam period can get a bit stressful with a lot of exams in few days.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people from all over the world, hearing their perspectives and experiences, and getting to know them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Course registration was difficult, and I wrote a lot of e-mails back and forth with many different employees, but again, I received a lot of help.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your time, it is such a nice city and you will for sure have a great time!:))

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
